course_name_original: Globalization. New Challenges in the Contemporary World
course_name_en: Globalization. New Challenges in the Contemporary World

learning_outcomes.text: Knows at a basic level the non-technical conditions of transformations occurring in the contemporary world in philosophical, cultural, economic, legal, historical, religious, political and social dimensions. Understands the functioning of contemporary society and its philosophical, cultural, economic, legal, historical, religious, political and social conditions.
Understands the principles of functioning of market mechanisms in the contemporary world.

Is able to work independently on a research problem based on self-selected scientific sources; is able to prepare an oral statement or written text on non-technical conditions of transformations occurring in society from a philosophical, cultural, economic, legal, historical, religious, political and social perspective.
Is able to integrate knowledge from various bibliographic sources and databases in Polish and English (or another language recognized as a language of international scientific communication).

Is able to write a scientific text in Polish and a foreign language (recognized as a language of international scientific communication), which is a well-documented bibliographic study of a given problem, in accordance with the requirements of substantive and linguistic correctness. Is able to characterize the transformations of contemporary society from a philosophical, cultural, legal, economic and social perspective based on self-selected scientific sources.
Is aware of the scope of their current knowledge and understands the need for continuous self-education and self-development.

Understands the consequences of technical and engineering activities in the natural and social environment. Is aware of responsibility for decisions made in the field of engineering activities. Demonstrates an pro-ecological attitude.

syllabus_topics: Economic aspects of globalization and modernization (global market and new economic rules; the issue of contemporary poverty and wealth; migrations; discussion of the 20/80 rule in post-industrial society). Anti-globalists' postulates.

Political aspects of globalization (Huntington's theory of the clash of civilizations and other related theories; contemporary conflicts and wars, terrorism; intercontinental migrations and their consequences; the future of the nation-state; the idea of democracy in confrontation with the contemporary market).

Cultural aspects of globalization (the issue of the "clash of civilizations", the impact of globalization processes on the formation of consumer society; interpersonal bonds in the era of globalization).
Demographic and ecological forecasts for the world - including the consequences of climate change.
Education for the future (prevention of intercultural conflicts; counteracting aggression and violence; ecological awareness, lifelong learning as a requirement of a new way of creating value).
Screenings of films and presentations illustrating the above problems.
